4. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the defendant No. 1 handed over all the necessary papers to the deed writer before writing and execution of the deed, but the deed writer inadvertently without writing correct dates mistakenly written wrong dates of the previous deeds in the disputed deed. The plaintiff did not file the suit within the time, as such the suit is barred by limitation and plaintiff is not entitled to get relief as prayed for. 

 5. The learned Assistant Judge, Dupchan-chia, Bogura dismissed the suit on the grounds that the plaintiff failed to prove the cause of action and prayer of the plaintiff for rectification of recital of the deed instead of schedule of the disputed land in the deed is not lawful. Against the said judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Dupchanchia, Bogura, the plaintiff preferred an appeal being No. 92 of 2018 before the learned District Judge, Bogura which was disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Bogura reversing the judgment and decree of the learned Assistant Judge, Dupchanchia on the grounds that the suit is not barred by limitation, the defendant in his testimony admitted that he has executed and registered the disputed deed and the plaintiff is in possession and he has no objection if the plaintiff rectify his deed through process of court- and accordingly, he allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree passed by the Assistant Judge. 

 7. Mr Abdul Kader Bhuiyan, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the suit is barred by limitation. The learned Assistant Judge rightly passed the judgment on consideration of the evidences on record but the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Bogura illegally reversed the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Dupchanchia, Bogura. He also submits that the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Bogura without considering the evidences and findings of the learned Assistant Judge allowed the appeal illegally and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 8. On the other hand, Mr Ashfaqur Rahman, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that the learned Assistant Judge wrongly and illegally dismissed the suit. He further submits that the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Bogura considering all the materials on record rightly and legally reversed the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge and decreed the original suit. He also submits that the suit is not barred by limitation and the defendant No. 1 admitted the execution and registration of sale deed No. 3405 dated 17-6-2008. He also admitted the possession of the plaintiff and the defendant has no objection if the plaintiffs rectify his deed through court. Under such circumstances he prayed for discharging the Rule. 

 10. Under such circumstances I am of the view that there was cause of action to file the suit and plaintiff filed the suit within the period of limitation three years under Article 96 of the Limitation Act, 1908. Article 96 provides provisions for filing a suit on the ground of mistake, where limitation is three years from the date when the mistake becomes known to the plaintiff Moreover, on perusal of the record it appears that the error in the present case is a mistake on behalf of both the parties, the vendor and the vendee that is mutual mistake of parties and their intention was to include the correct year and dates of the previous three deeds in the disputed deed No. 3405 dated 17-6-2008 but inadvertently the deed writer wrote the incorrect year and dates concerned in the said disputed deed. Here the court is authorize by law to exercise its discretion to rectify the disputed deed so as to express the real intention of the parties under section 31 of the Specific Relief Act. In this case this rectification can be done without prejudice to the rights acquired by the third person in good faith, inasmuch as in the instant case there is no third person who claims rights acquired in good faith and for value. In fact, in this case, there is no third person/party claimant. Moreover, the defendant-petitioner conceded the execution and registration of the disputed deed where in the mutual mistake was committed. Even the defendant in his written statement admitted that the mistake was committed inadvertently by the deed writer. Therefore, the section 31 of the Specific Relief Act, permits the plaintiff to have the instrument rectified since there is mutual mistake of both the parties which was detected on 12-10-2014 and the plaintiff filed the suit on 1-9-2015 with the statutory period of limitation. So the suit is maintainable and it is not barred by limitation. 

 12. As per facts of the above case the suit for rectification was filed after a long period of time, in that suit his Lordship decided that at any time when a mistake is discovered or fraud comes to light it is open to the parties affected to institute a suit for the rectification of mistake in the instrument. But in the instant suit the suit was not filed after a long time of the commission of mistake and knowledge of mistake, rather the plaintiff came to know about the mistake on 12-10-2014 and filed the suit on 1-9-2015. So, undoubtedly it can be said that the instant suit is not barred by limitation in the light of the above mentioned decision and discussions. The appellate court rightly decided that the suit is not barred by limitation. The learned Assistant Judge is misconceived in law that the suit is barred by limitation. He is also misconceived in law that the plaintiff did not come to the court to rectify the schedule of the deed rather he has illegally come to rectify the recital made in the body of the deed. For that reason he took his view in favour of the defendant which is fully illegal inasmuch as there is no bar in section 31 of the Specific Relief Act to rectify the recital of the deed contained mistake in its body.
